subject.title: [Bug] Dreaming narrative: hardcoded 60s timeout includes lane-queue wait; timeout disposal aborts the primary call then discards the successful fallback-model output

question: Should memory-core keep one fixed bounded narrative deadline, or support a bounded user-configurable/per-phase deadline while separating timeout cleanup from the ownership of an in-flight result?
rationale: The implementation must choose a public plugin configuration contract and a deliberate lifecycle policy for runs that exceed the caller wait without treating the current fallback-and-delete sequence as an incidental implementation detail.

options.title: Define lifecycle first, then bounded config
options.body: Make timeout completion and session disposal non-destructive to a valid late result, then add a validated bounded timeout setting with focused upgrade and runtime proof.

options.title: Keep one fixed deadline
options.body: Retain a global fixed limit but move queue admission outside the timed window and document that slow providers may receive a fallback after that bound.

options.title: Treat as performance-only
options.body: Rely on the no-tools and concurrency work without adding timeout control, accepting that slow local and queued runs can still fall back at the fixed limit.

recommendation.title: Define lifecycle first, then bounded config
recommendation.body: Make timeout completion and session disposal non-destructive to a valid late result, then add a validated bounded timeout setting with focused upgrade and runtime proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The choice changes bundled-plugin product policy and public configuration surface, and the available Dreaming and vision evidence points to this project-direction owner.
